purpose: Manual semantic alignment between the independently-discovered low-effort (22) and high-effort (34) GPT-5.5 model-defined feature sets. Used only to build a fair matched-pair low-vs-high comparison; the underlying scoring, output files, and frozen feature sets used for scoring are unchanged.
method: Human/assistant judgment matching feature definitions by shared underlying construct, not by name string similarity. Not every feature has a match; unmatched features are condition-specific and are reported separately, never forced into a pair.

pairs.rationale: Both track planning/enforcing a specific target number of references.
Both prioritize or filter candidates by direct topical relevance.
Both express intent to avoid fabricated/non-real references.
Both describe checking/verifying bibliographic accuracy before presenting citations.
Both concern how much bibliographic detail (authors, venue, year, etc.) to include.
Both concern choosing/attending to a citation style or format.
Both plan short notes explaining why each reference is relevant.
Both seek classic/foundational works, high-effort framing it as a deliberate balance with contemporary work.
Both use the focal paper's date to restrict or prioritize reference timing.
Both decompose the topic into subthemes and plan coverage across them.
Both consider mixing different kinds of sources (papers, books, reviews, guidelines).
Both adapt the bibliography plan to the user's stated or inferred request.
Both mark citation details/relevance as uncertain rather than asserting them confidently.
Both stress thoroughness/completeness sufficient to form a solid research foundation.
Both target references tied to specific methods/techniques used in the focal field.
Both plan a structured reference list; the high-effort definition specifically emphasizes numbering.
